title: How to Arrange Potted Plants Like a Garden Designer
h1: How to Arrange Potted Plants: Groupings, Heights and Pot Choices for Balconies and Patios
description: Learn how to arrange potted plants with thriller-filler-spiller, odd-number groupings and height layering, plus pot sizes, materials, drainage and sun tips.
excerpt: Group pots in odd numbers, layer heights and repeat materials: a step-by-step guide to arranging potted plants on balconies, patios and steps.
image_alt: Group of potted plants arranged in three heights on a balcony, with an olive tree, ornamental grass and trailing ivy in matching planters
key_takeaways: Group pots in odd numbers, usually three or five, with the tallest at the back or in the corner.
Use thriller-filler-spiller in pots 14 in. wide or larger: one tall plant, three fillers, two or three trailers.
Repeat one pot material or color to make a group look intentional.
Cluster plants that share the same sun and water needs so care is easier.
Every pot needs a drainage hole; skip the gravel layer and use potting mix all the way down.

faq.q: How do you group potted plants together?
faq.a: Group potted plants in odd numbers, usually three or five, starting with the largest pot as an anchor at the back or in a corner. Layer medium and short pots in front so the tops form a loose triangle, vary leaf shapes and textures, and repeat one pot color or material. Let foliage overlap slightly so the group reads as one arrangement.

faq.q: What is the thriller, filler, spiller method?
faq.a: It is a container planting formula. The thriller is one tall focal plant in the center or back, such as an ornamental grass. Fillers are mounded mid-height plants like geraniums or coleus that surround it. Spillers are trailing plants like sweet potato vine or ivy planted near the rim to cascade over the edge. All three should share the same light and water needs.

faq.q: Should you put gravel in the bottom of plant pots?
faq.a: Generally no. A gravel layer does not improve drainage and can actually raise the saturated zone in the soil, leaving roots wetter. Instead, use a pot with a drainage hole, place a piece of mesh or a coffee filter over the hole to hold soil in, and fill the pot with quality potting mix all the way down.

faq.q: How many plants should I put on a small balcony?
faq.a: There is no set number, but fewer and larger pots usually look better and are easier to care for than many small ones. On a typical small balcony, one tall group of three in a corner plus a trough along the railing or wall is plenty. Keep a clear path from the door and check your building's weight limits first.

faq.q: What pots are best for a balcony?
faq.a: Lightweight fiberglass, resin and fiber-cement pots are the best choices for balconies because they are durable, frost tolerant and far lighter than stone or concrete. Choose pots with drainage holes and use saucers or self-watering reservoirs so water does not drip onto balconies below. Wide-based shapes resist tipping in the wind.
